the bytes this model does not name (+0x02..+0x11 combat position and orders, +0x16, +0x18..+0x21, +0x23, +0x4A, +0x4D/+0x4E, +0x52..+0x54, +0x56/+0x57, +0x59, +0x7F) are kept as read (Character.OriginalRecord); a character made by this program has zeros there. some sets (battlefield 0x38's floor decorations: record 23 of a 5680-byte .ffc, second frame 0x1B40) give a second frame past the end of the decoded file; the original points into whatever follows the block. No second frame here.

the format is read from the data (every BC tile parses exactly within its record size, IMC frames as the old engine's CleanCombatPreparedPresentation does); whether the first byte is width − 1 or a hot spot for IMC frames is not settled, so nothing relies on Width for frames.
(0, 0) here when a game is begun or loaded from the opening screen; the original's value then (the program's start, or a battle of the game played before) was not traced.
the original scrolls once per pass of its loop, which runs as fast as the redraw allows; here once a frame.

a clock() tick as one millisecond (MSC 6 CLK_TCK = 1000); the 0410 timer ticks have another unit, see MessageBox and Cinematics.
the selection bytes are taken to be 0 outside a battle (the panel is drawn unlit everywhere else, PartyPanel.Draw).

the horizontal centring uses (320 - text width - w->w) / 2 relative to the window; the window offset w->w of card_window is taken as 60 (the card window starts right of the party panel), so the box is centred on the 260 pixels right of the panel. The offset was not checked at run time (it could be 0 when a box comes up over a full screen such as the start screen).
the length of a 0410 timer tick. 1000 ms assumes 60 ticks per second; the PAN player's measured tick (86 ms per 6 ticks, see Cinematics) would give 860 ms.
what sound_play(2) and (3) do; they are not played here.
one tick after the last cel of OPENING2 (the capture's tick after it came in the same frame, before the tune).
a clock() tick is taken as one millisecond (MSC 6 CLK_TCK is 1000, although the value only changes every 55 ms with the BIOS timer, so a real pass lasts 30 to 55 ms).
hosts may not deliver Shift-Tab as 0x0F00 (the BIOS code); then only Tab steps.
SI is taken to come through the thunk 09C0:1EE1 unchanged (the overlay manager is taken to keep it).
the driver's AX is taken never to be 0x11B (it would end the screen).
root 0000:24BC is taken to be the framed message box MessageBox shows (60 ticks there).

the text routine root 0265:0134 is assembly only: the name is taken as centred in its 154-pixel column with the capital at y 8 (positions from a capture of the original), the description as wrapped in 156 pixels from (0x94, 0x25).
the names are drawn by the text routine (assembly only) in a 52-pixel column; here each full name is cut to fit that width on its row.
